problemText: A triangle has a base of 10 meters and a height of 8 meters, where the height is measured perpendicular to the base. What is the area of the triangle?
choices: 18 square meters
80 square meters
40 square meters
160 square meters
hints: Remember that area of a triangle equals base times height divided by two.
Start by multiplying the base and height together, then divide that product in half.

problemText: A parallelogram has a base of 12 inches. The straight up-and-down distance between the parallelogram's two parallel sides is 7 inches. One of the slanted sides of the parallelogram measures 9 inches. What is the area of the parallelogram?
choices: 126 square inches
108 square inches
63 square inches
84 square inches
hints: Think about which measurement tells you how tall the parallelogram is — perpendicular to the base.
The slanted side length is a distractor; you need the perpendicular distance, not the slant.

problemText: Marcus is drawing a triangle on grid paper. He chooses a base of the triangle that is 9 centimeters long. He measures the perpendicular distance from that base to the opposite corner and finds it is 6 centimeters. What is the area of Marcus's triangle, in square centimeters?
choices: 27 square centimeters
54 square centimeters
15 square centimeters
45 square centimeters
hints: Use the triangle area rule: base times height, then divide by two.
Make sure you divide by two after multiplying; that is the key step that makes it a triangle and not a rectangle.

problemText: A composite shape is made of a rectangle and a triangle sitting on top of it. The rectangle has a width of 6 inches and a height of 5 inches. On top of the rectangle, a triangle has the same 6-inch width as the rectangle's top edge for its base, and the triangle's height, measured perpendicular to that base, is 4 inches. What is the total area of the entire composite shape?
choices: 30 square inches
42 square inches
12 square inches
72 square inches
hints: Decompose the shape into two pieces: find the area of the rectangle and the area of the triangle separately.
Add the areas of the two pieces together to get the total area of the whole shape.

problemText: A trapezoid-shaped garden bed can be decomposed by drawing a vertical line from one corner of the shape to the opposite side. This creates a rectangle and a triangle. The rectangle part is 8 meters wide and 3 meters tall. The triangle part has a base of 2 meters and a height of 3 meters, measured perpendicular to its base. What is the total area of the garden bed?
choices: 24 square meters
48 square meters
27 square meters
30 square meters
hints: Find the area of the rectangle using length times width.
Find the area of the triangle using base times height divided by two, then add the two areas together.

problemText: A large rectangle is 10 inches wide and 8 inches tall. From one corner of the rectangle, a right triangle is cut away. The triangle has a base of 4 inches and a height of 8 inches, measured perpendicular to that base. You can think of the remaining shape as the big rectangle with a triangular piece removed. What is the area of the shape that remains after the triangle is cut away?
choices: 96 square inches
80 square inches
16 square inches
64 square inches
hints: Start by finding the area of the whole large rectangle before anything is removed.
Then find the area of the triangle that was cut away, and subtract it from the rectangle's area.

problemText: A net is a flat pattern that unfolds from a three-dimensional solid. When you fold a net back up, what do the shared edges in the net represent?
choices: The sides of the solid that are hidden from view
The edges where two faces of the solid meet
The seams where the solid will be glued together
Extra material left over after the solid is formed
hints: Think about what happens physically when you fold a net along those shared edges.
In the net, a shared edge belongs to two different flat shapes — what happens to those two shapes when folded?

problemText: A rectangular prism has length 8 cm, width 5 cm, and height 3 cm. The net of this prism will contain six rectangles arranged in three matching pairs. What are the dimensions of the rectangle that forms the top and bottom faces of the prism?
choices: 3 cm by 5 cm
8 cm by 3 cm
8 cm by 5 cm
5 cm by 3 cm
hints: The top and bottom of the box run the full length and width of the prism.
Neither the height of 3 cm nor any shorter dimension forms the edges of the top face.

problemText: A triangular prism has two identical right-triangle ends with legs 6 inches and 8 inches, and a hypotenuse of 10 inches. The prism is 12 inches long. In the net, there will be three rectangles connecting the two triangular ends. Which statement correctly describes the widths of these three rectangles?
choices: All three rectangles have the same width of 12 inches
The three rectangles have widths of 8 inches, 10 inches, and 12 inches
The three rectangles have widths of 6 inches, 6 inches, and 8 inches
The three rectangles have widths of 6 inches, 8 inches, and 10 inches
hints: Each rectangular side wraps around one side of the triangular end — what dimension of the triangle does each rectangle's width match?
The triangle has three sides: the two legs and the hypotenuse. Each becomes the width of one rectangle.

problemText: A small box shaped like a rectangular prism has dimensions 7 inches long, 4 inches wide, and 3 inches tall. To find the total surface area using the net, a student must find the area of each of the six rectangles in the net and add them. However, the student only added the areas of four rectangles: the top (28 sq in), the bottom (28 sq in), the front (21 sq in), and the back (21 sq in). What is the total surface area, and why was the student's method incomplete?
choices: The total is 122 sq in. The student forgot to add the two end rectangles that are 12 sq in each.
The total is 98 sq in. The student forgot to add the two end rectangles that are 12 sq in each.
The total is 152 sq in. The student forgot to add the two end rectangles that are 24 sq in each.
The total is 98 sq in. The student double-counted the top and bottom rectangles.
hints: Count all six faces of a rectangular prism: you have top, bottom, front, back, and two more. What are those two missing faces?
The two missing rectangles connect the front and back to the ends of the box. Their dimensions are the width (4 in) and height (3 in).

problemText: A triangular prism pencil case has two identical right-triangle ends with legs 5 cm and 12 cm, and a hypotenuse of 13 cm. The prism is 20 cm long. A student correctly found that each triangular end has an area of 30 square centimeters. She then found the areas of the three rectangles: 100 sq cm, 240 sq cm, and 260 sq cm. What is the total surface area of the pencil case?
choices: 570 square centimeters
660 square centimeters
600 square centimeters
630 square centimeters
hints: A triangular prism has two triangular faces and three rectangular faces. Make sure you include both triangular ends in your final sum.
Add both triangular ends (each is 30 sq cm) to all three rectangles.

problemText: An artist is building a cardboard model of a triangular prism. She needs to cut out a net from a single sheet of cardboard and fold it without any overlaps. The triangular ends are right triangles with legs 4 units and 3 units, and a hypotenuse of 5 units. The prism is 8 units long. Before she cuts, she wants to verify that her net design is correct by checking that every shared edge in the net has matching length on both sides. Which pair of edge lengths would indicate a mistake in the net design that would prevent it from folding into the correct prism?
choices: A 4-unit edge of a triangle matching a 4-unit edge of a rectangle
A 3-unit edge of a triangle matching a 3-unit edge of a rectangle
A 5-unit edge of a triangle matching an edge of a rectangle that is 8 units long
The 8-unit height of one rectangle matching the 8-unit height of another rectangle
hints: For the net to fold correctly, each side of the triangle must match the width of exactly one rectangle, and the length of every rectangle must be the same as the prism's length.
A 5-unit side of the triangle cannot attach to a rectangle that is 8 units wide. What should the width of that rectangle be?

problemText: A polygon is a closed, flat shape made only of straight sides with no gaps or curves. The corner points of a polygon are called vertices. When drawing a polygon from a list of coordinates, what must you do after connecting all the vertices in order to the next vertex?
choices: Draw a diagonal line across the middle of the shape
Erase the line from the first vertex to the second vertex
Leave the shape open so you can add more vertices later
Connect the last vertex back to the first vertex to close the shape
hints: Think about what makes a polygon different from just a connected path with loose ends.
A polygon must be closed with one final segment connecting the last vertex back to where you started.

problemText: A rectangular garden has corners at vertices A(4, 2), B(4, 7), C(9, 7), and D(9, 2), where each unit is one meter. Side AB connects A and B. What is the length of side AB?
choices: 5 meters
6 meters
4 meters
9 meters
hints: Check which coordinate is the same for both A and B to see if this side is horizontal or vertical.
Once you know the side direction, use absolute value to find each vertex's distance from zero, then combine those distances.

problemText: Two consecutive vertices of a polygon are located at P(6, -2) and Q(6, 5). The side PQ connects these two vertices. Is side PQ horizontal or vertical, and how do you know?
choices: Side PQ is horizontal because both vertices share the same second coordinate of -2
Side PQ is vertical because both vertices share the same first coordinate of 6
Side PQ is horizontal because the y-coordinate changes from -2 to 5
Side PQ is vertical because the y-coordinate changes from -2 to 5
hints: Look at which coordinate stays the same between the two vertices.
When the first coordinate (x-coordinate) is the same for both points, the side is vertical. When the second coordinate (y-coordinate) is the same for both points, the side is horizontal.

problemText: A polygon has vertices at R(-3, 4), S(-3, -2), T(5, -2), and U(5, 4), listed in order. Each unit represents one centimeter. Draw the shape and find the length of side ST. Show your work by identifying which coordinates change and which stay the same.
choices: Side ST is horizontal with a length of 6 centimeters
Side ST is vertical with a length of 6 centimeters
Side ST is horizontal with a length of 8 centimeters
Side ST is vertical with a length of 8 centimeters
hints: First identify what S and T share: do they have the same first coordinate or the same second coordinate?
After identifying the direction, find the distance by looking at the coordinate that differs and checking whether the vertices are on the same side of zero or opposite sides.

problemText: A hexagon has six vertices listed in order: M(-5, 3), N(-5, -4), O(2, -4), P(2, 1), Q(6, 1), and R(6, 3). Each unit is one foot. To draw this polygon correctly, you plot all six vertices and then connect them in order, finishing by connecting R back to M. Calculate the length of side MN.
choices: Side MN is 9 feet long because you add the distances from zero: |3| + |-4| = 3 + 4 = 9
Side MN is 2 feet long because you subtract the first coordinates: |-5| − |-5| = 0, then measure vertically
Side MN is 1 foot long because the first coordinates are identical and the second coordinates differ by one unit
Side MN is 7 feet long because M and N share the same first coordinate and are on opposite sides of zero
hints: Check which coordinate M and N share to determine the side direction.
Since this side is vertical, use the second coordinates and check whether 3 and -4 sit on the same side of zero or opposite sides to decide whether to add or subtract.

problemText: A polygon shaped like a backwards L has vertices at V(-2, 5), W(-2, -3), X(3, -3), Y(3, 2), Z(1, 2), and A(1, 5), listed in order. Each unit is one yard. To draw the complete polygon, you must plot all six vertices and connect them in the order given, then connect A back to V. Three of the six sides are VW, WX, and XY. Calculate the lengths of all three sides and determine which side is the longest.
choices: Side VW is 8 yards, side WX is 5 yards, and side XY is 5 yards; VW is the longest
Side VW is 8 yards, side WX is 5 yards, and side XY is 5 yards; WX and XY are tied for longest
Side VW is 3 yards, side WX is 8 yards, and side XY is 5 yards; WX is the longest
Side VW is 8 yards, side WX is 6 yards, and side XY is 5 yards; VW is the longest
hints: For each side, first identify which coordinate stays the same to determine the direction, then use absolute value and the zero-crossing rule to find the length.

For VW: V and W share the first coordinate -2, so use the second coordinates 5 and -3, which are on opposite sides of zero; for WX: W and X share the second coordinate -3, so use the first coordinates -2 and 3, which are on opposite sides of zero; for XY: X and Y share the first coordinate 3, so use the second coordinates -3 and 2, which are on opposite sides of zero.

problemText: A unit cube has an edge length of exactly 1 unit. If you stack unit cubes to fill a rectangular prism completely with no gaps or leftover cubes, what does the total number of cubes you use represent?
choices: The volume of the rectangular prism, measured in cubic units
The surface area of the rectangular prism, measured in square units
The perimeter of the rectangular prism, measured in linear units
The height of the rectangular prism, measured in one direction only
hints: Volume is about filling the entire inside space of a solid.
Think about what the definition of volume means in terms of cubes that pack a shape.

problemText: A right rectangular prism has edge lengths of 4 inches, 3 inches, and 2 inches. How many unit cubes, each with an edge length of 1 inch, will fit inside this prism with no gaps and no cubes sticking out?
choices: 18 unit cubes
24 unit cubes
12 unit cubes
9 unit cubes
hints: The formula V = length × width × height counts layers of unit cubes.
Multiply the three edge lengths together: 4 × 3 × 2.

problemText: A small cube has an edge length of 1/3 inch. What is the volume of this small cube?
choices: 1/3 cubic inch
1/9 cubic inch
1/27 cubic inch
3 cubic inches
hints: Volume of a cube is calculated by multiplying edge length times edge length times edge length.
Multiply the fractions: (1/3) × (1/3) × (1/3).

problemText: A rectangular prism has edge lengths of 1/2 inch, 1/2 inch, and 1/4 inch. You want to pack this prism with small cubes that all have the same edge length, with no gaps and no leftover space. First, choose an edge length that fits a whole number of times along every edge of the prism. Then, calculate how many of those small cubes will fit inside the prism.
choices: 2 small cubes, each with edge length 1/2 inch
4 small cubes, each with edge length 1/4 inch
16 small cubes, each with edge length 1/8 inch
8 small cubes, each with edge length 1/4 inch
hints: The edge length you choose must divide evenly into all three edges of the prism: 1/2 inch, 1/2 inch, and 1/4 inch.
Once you pick the cube size, divide each edge of the prism by that cube size to count how many cubes fit along each direction, then multiply those three counts together.

problemText: A rectangular block measures 3/4 inch long, 2 inches wide, and 1/2 inch tall. Two students calculate its volume differently. Student A packs the block with small cubes and counts them, then multiplies by the volume of one small cube. Student B multiplies the three edge lengths directly using the formula V = l × w × h. Should their final answers be the same, or will one of them be wrong?
choices: Their answers should be the same; packing cubes and multiplying edges always agree for any rectangular prism.
Student A will get a larger answer because counting individual cubes gives a more accurate result than multiplying fractions.
Student B will get a smaller answer because the formula V = l × w × h does not work with fractional edges.
Their answers will differ because one method counts layers while the other counts individual cubes.
hints: When you pack a rectangular prism with small cubes of equal size and count them carefully, multiplying the count by the volume of each small cube produces the same result as multiplying the three edge lengths together.
The volume formula V = l × w × h works whether the edge lengths are whole numbers or fractions. If you count small unit cubes and multiply by each cube's volume, you will get exactly the same answer.

problemText: A rectangular prism has edge lengths of 5/3 inches, 3/2 inches, and 1/2 inch. You decide to pack this prism with small unit-fraction cubes, where each small cube has edge length 1/6 inch. After you pack the prism, you count 90 small cubes. Without unpacking, verify that your count is correct by calculating the total volume of all 90 small cubes and comparing it to the volume found by multiplying the prism's three edge lengths directly. Are the two volumes equal?
choices: Yes, both methods give 15/8 cubic inches, so the count of 90 is correct.
Yes, both methods give 5/4 cubic inches, so the count of 90 is correct.
No, packing gives 90/216 cubic inches but the formula gives 5/4 cubic inches, so the count is wrong.
No, packing gives 1.25 cubic inches but the formula gives 1.875 cubic inches, so the count is wrong.
hints: First, find the volume of one small cube with edge length 1/6 inch: multiply (1/6) × (1/6) × (1/6). Then multiply by 90 to get the total volume from packing. Compare that to (5/3) × (3/2) × (1/2).
When you multiply (5/3) × (3/2) × (1/2), group the numerators and denominators separately: (5 × 3 × 1) over (3 × 2 × 2).
